title: DATE Data Type
description: Learn how to use the DATE data type to store date values in SQL Server.

data.text: The DATE data type stores only the date component (no time). The range is from January 1, 1 CE to December 31, 9999 CE.
It takes 3 bytes to store a DATE value. The default literal string format is YYYY-MM-DD.

data.title: Query by DATE Value
data.code:
SELECT     
    order_id, 
    customer_id, 
    order_status, 
    order_date
FROM     
    sales.orders
WHERE order_date < '2016-01-05'
ORDER BY 
    order_date DESC;

data.title: DATE Columns in a Table
data.content: Creates a table with DATE columns for validity periods.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE sales.list_prices (
    product_id INT NOT NULL,
    valid_from DATE NOT NULL,
    valid_to DATE NOT NULL,
    amount DEC (10, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (product_id, valid_from, valid_to),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) 
      REFERENCES production.products (product_id)
);

data.text: `DATE` stores only the calendar date. Use `DATEADD` to move through time and `DATEDIFF` to measure the distance between two dates; both are cheap and index-friendly when you avoid wrapping an indexed column in a function.

data.title: Date functions you will actually use
data.content: The final query shows the sargable range-filter pattern that lets SQL Server use an index on the date column.
data.code:
SELECT
    DATEFROMPARTS(2024, 2, 29)                AS leap_day,     -- 2024-02-29
    EOMONTH('2024-02-10')                     AS end_of_month, -- 2024-02-29
    DATEADD(DAY, -7, CAST(GETDATE() AS DATE)) AS one_week_ago,
    DATEDIFF(YEAR, '1990-06-15', GETDATE())   AS age_in_years;

-- Sargable half-open range (uses an index on order_date when one exists)
DECLARE @start DATE = '2024-01-01', @end DATE = '2024-02-01';

SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_in_january
FROM sales.orders
WHERE order_date >= @start
  AND order_date <  @end;

data.title: Avoid this anti-pattern
data.text: `WHERE YEAR(order_date) = 2024` wraps the indexed column in a function, so SQL Server cannot seek the index and scans the table instead. Prefer a half-open range: `order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date < '2025-01-01'.

data.title: DATE Key Points
points: DATE stores only the date component (no time).
Use DATE when you only need to store dates, not times.
